classifications: Theory of computation → Data structures design and analysis
statement: Could our technique be extended to obtain lock-free implementations of sequential augmented data structures that require more complex updates (such as the insertion of a pair of keys)? In the sequential setting, examples of such data structures include link/cut trees [41] and segment trees [9, 10]. Shafiei [40] described a mechanism for making multiple changes to a tree appear atomic, but it would require additional work to find a suitable way to generalize our Propagate routine with her approach.
context: Although we base our augmented BST on [21], we believe our technique could also be applied to the similar lock-free BST design of Natarajan, Ramachandran and Mittal [35] or other concurrent trees. It would be interesting to apply it to a node-oriented tree such as [27], a balanced tree such as the lock-free chromatic BST of [15] or to a self-balancing concurrent tree such as the CB Tree [2]. In particular, the latter two would require ensuring the Propagate routine works correctly with rotations used to rebalance the tree. The technique may also be applicable to trees that use other coordination mechanisms, such as locks (e.g., [35]).
